answer:
**Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS) 2013‑2023 – Experiencing Violence**

In the **“Trend (All Years Available)”** table of the Experiencing Violence section of the *Youth Risk Behavior Survey Data Summary & Trends Report 2013‑2023* (available through CDC WONDER), a “Wrong Direction” flag is used whenever an overall trend shows a **rise in prevalence** over the full decade.

| # | Sub‑category (Experiencing Violence) | Trend | Wrong Direction |
|---|--------------------------------------|-------|-----------------|
| 1 | Victim of violent crime | Increasing | **Yes** |
| 2 | Victim of violent injury from a **fight** | Increasing | **Yes** |
| 3 | Victim of violent injury from a **non‑fight** | Increasing | **Yes** |
| 4 | Victim of **sexual violence** | Increasing | **Yes** |

These four items are the only ones in the Experiencing Violence section that were flagged as trending in the wrong direction (i.e., showing increased prevalence) from 2013 to 2023.

*Source:* CDC WONDER – *Youth Risk Behavior Survey Data Summary & Trends Report 2013‑2023* (PDF).  
Link: <https://www.cdc.gov/violenceprevention/youth-risk-behavior/_downloads/yrbs-data-summary-trends-2013-2023.pdf>
